goal_text: (Reused from sequential_017) A factory must schedule jobs A, B, C, D, E (each takes 1 hour, no parallel execution). Constraints: A must complete before both B and C; B must complete before D; C must complete before E. How many valid orderings exist? List all of them.
ground_truth: A must be first. Remaining: B,C,D,E in positions 2-5 with B<D and C<E. Count of valid 4-permutations with both B<D and C<E: 4!/4 = 6. All 6 orderings: (1)A,B,C,D,E; (2)A,B,C,E,D; (3)A,B,D,C,E; (4)A,C,B,D,E; (5)A,C,B,E,D; (6)A,C,E,B,D.
